bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The saved 5276-byte witness is evaluated by QuickJS only because its last byte is `0x00`; `JS_Eval` then parses the first 5275 bytes using explicit `input_len`, so internal zero bytes remain in-band. The saved crash stack proves the accepted program executes at least one `OP_for_in_start`, so some accepted `for..in` path reaches `build_for_in_iterator`, but the preserved artifacts do not identify which witness-side `for`/`in` fragment produced that opcode or what `JSValue` occupied `sp[-1]`. On the crashing path, `build_for_in_iterator` bypasses its null/undefined early return and its `slow_path`, then reinterprets the unresolved `obj` operand as `JSObject *` at line 15129 and immediately reads `p->fast_array` at line 15131. AddressSanitizer reports that one-byte read at `0x607000000005`, 27 bytes to the left of the 72-byte region `[0x607000000020,0x607000000068)` allocated in `JS_NewObjectFromShape`. The saved artifacts therefore ground the parser admission, an executed `for..in` opcode, the fast-path control decisions, the sink-adjacent unchecked cast, and the crashing read, but they do not reveal whether the bogus pointer state was already present in `sp[-1]` or arose earlier inside the helper.

tainted_value_origin.code: JSValue val = JS_Eval(ctx, (const char *)Data, Size-1, "<none>", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL);
tainted_value_origin.description: The libFuzzer harness passes the exact witness buffer to QuickJS as script source, using `Size - 1` as the explicit script length after first checking that `Data[Size - 1] == 0`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 5276 bytes with SHA-256 `b908cea89fbf8c247b50d6718e120612ee1f904233f6a469a247b3d3a310f9d6`. Because the reproduced run crashed, byte 5275 is the required NUL terminator; QuickJS receives the first 5275 bytes as source and, because it also receives an explicit `input_len`, any internal `0x00` bytes remain part of the parsed buffer instead of terminating it.

source.description: First project parser step that materializes the attacker-controlled witness as an explicit bounded byte range. Any accepted `for..in` syntax later compiled to the crashing `OP_for_in_start` is read from this `[buf_ptr, buf_end)` span.
source.value_from: This step aliases the exact 5275-byte script slice of the saved 5276-byte witness. QuickJS uses `buf_end` rather than `strlen`, so internal zero bytes remain in-band and only the final byte serves as the harness-required terminator.

root_cause.description: Sink-adjacent unchecked reinterpretation of the runtime enumeration operand as `JSObject *`.
root_cause.note: This is the latest source line the saved artifacts ground before the sink. They show the cast feeds the crashing `p->fast_array` read, but they do not establish whether the bogus pointer was already in `sp[-1]` or was produced by an earlier statement inside `build_for_in_iterator`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The first dereference after the unchecked cast reads the one-byte `fast_array` bitfield and produces the saved heap-buffer-overflow read.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `quickjs.c:15131` on address `0x607000000005`, 27 bytes to the left of the 72-byte region `[0x607000000020,0x607000000068)`, matching this one-byte `p->fast_array` access.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crash stack reaches `JS_EvalFunctionInternal` and `JS_CallInternal`, so `js_parse_program()` necessarily succeeded and emitted executable bytecode. Because frame 1 is `js_for_in_start`, at least one accepted `for..in` path reached `js_parse_for_in_of()` and emitted `OP_for_in_start`, though the exact witness fragment is not preserved.

evidence_limitations: The saved `poc` contains multiple `for`/`in`-looking fragments, and no Stage 01 artifact records which one compiled into the crashing `OP_for_in_start`. With `run_flags.json` setting `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, the trace can only name an accepted `for..in` path, not a unique witness-side loop head or RHS expression.

No saved artifact records the runtime `JSValue` bits in `sp[-1]` or any source-level mutation of local `obj` inside `build_for_in_iterator`. The trace therefore stops at the sink-adjacent `p = JS_VALUE_GET_OBJ(obj)` cast and the subsequent `p->fast_array` read rather than asserting where the bogus pointer state was created.

The packaged metadata `fixed_commit` / `patch.diff` do not modify `build_for_in_iterator`, `js_for_in_start`, `js_parse_for_in_of`, or any related `for..in` logic. `patch_resolves` is therefore false and the chain is grounded by the staged vulnerable source plus `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `reproduction_report.json`, not by a matching fix hunk.

coarse_trace.summary: QuickJS binds the exact 5275-byte script slice of the witness to an explicit `[buf_ptr, buf_end)` parser range and accepts it as executable source.
An accepted `for..in` path takes the `TOK_IN` branch and emits `OP_for_in_start`, but the exact witness-side loop head and RHS are not recoverable from the saved artifacts.
At runtime that emitted `OP_for_in_start` executes and passes an unresolved enumeration operand in `sp[-1]` into `build_for_in_iterator`.

The helper stays off its null/undefined return and `slow_path`, then casts the unresolved operand to `JSObject *` and crashes on the first `p->fast_array` read; the saved artifacts do not show where that bogus pointer state originated.

fine_trace.code: JSValue val = JS_Eval(ctx, (const char *)Data, Size-1, "<none>", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL);
fine_trace.note: The harness evaluates the exact witness buffer as QuickJS source only after checking `Data[Size - 1] == 0`. On the reproduced path this means the final byte is a terminator and the first 5275 bytes are handed to project code with an explicit length.

Source. `js_parse_init` creates a bounded parser view over the exact 5275-byte script slice of the witness. Because parsing is bounded by `buf_end`, internal `0x00` bytes remain in-band instead of terminating the input.

During compilation of some accepted loop head, `js_parse_for_in_of` sees `TOK_IN` rather than `of`, so it selects the `for..in` path. The saved crash stack proves this branch was taken at least once, but the preserved artifacts do not map a unique witness byte range to this token.
The compiler emits the runtime enumeration opcode for that accepted `for..in` path. This grounds the parser-to-bytecode transition without identifying a unique witness-side RHS expression.

When `JS_CallInternal` executes that opcode, `js_for_in_start` receives the loop's enumeration operand in `sp[-1]` and passes it into `build_for_in_iterator`. The saved artifacts do not recover which witness-side expression produced this slot or its raw `JSValue` bits.

`build_for_in_iterator` classifies the runtime operand by tag and boxes only primitive non-null/non-undefined inputs with `JS_ToObjectFree`. The saved artifacts do not reveal whether the crashing operand entered as an object or as a primitive that was boxed here.

fine_trace.code:
if (tag == JS_TAG_NULL || tag == JS_TAG_UNDEFINED)
    return enum_obj;
fine_trace.note: The crashing path does not take the null/undefined early return, so execution continues past this guard with an operand whose original tag was not `JS_TAG_NULL` or `JS_TAG_UNDEFINED`.

During the prototype-scan fast path, the helper would abandon this path if any visited prototype exposed enumerable keys. Reaching line 15129 proves `tab_atom_count == 0` on every visited prototype and that neither `slow_path` nor `fail` fired.

Sink-adjacent unchecked cast. After the fast-path checks in step 7, the code reinterprets the unresolved runtime operand `obj` as `JSObject *` without validating that it still denotes a live object layout. The saved artifacts ground this cast and the following sink, but they do not establish where the bogus pointer state originated.

ASan sink. The saved crash reports `READ of size 1` at `quickjs.c:15131` on address `0x607000000005`, 27 bytes to the left of the 72-byte region `[0x607000000020,0x607000000068)`, matching this one-byte `p->fast_array` access.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially. The saved artifacts ground the attacker bytes through `js_parse_init`, an accepted `for..in` branch, emitted `OP_for_in_start`, the runtime `sp[-1]` handoff into `build_for_in_iterator`, the fast-path control decisions, and the final `p->fast_array` sink. They do not identify the exact witness-side loop/RHS or where the bogus pointer state feeding `p = JS_VALUE_GET_OBJ(obj)` was created.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The packaged metadata `fixed_commit` / `patch.diff` add `findLast{Index}` support and do not modify `build_for_in_iterator`, `js_for_in_start`, `js_parse_for_in_of`, or any neighboring `for..in` logic on the reproduced crash path.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The provided `patch.diff` adds `Array.prototype.findLast`, `Array.prototype.findLastIndex`, and related unscopables entries. It does not touch `build_for_in_iterator`, `js_for_in_start`, the `for..in` compiler, or any other line named in the saved ASan trace.

key_changes.change: Adds `findLast{Index}` modes and updates `Array.prototype[Symbol.unscopables]`; unrelated to the reproduced `for..in` crash.

format.name: Exact 5276-byte NUL-terminated QuickJS script witness
format.contract: Exactly the saved blob at `gt_results/arvo_46701/poc` with SHA-256 `b908cea89fbf8c247b50d6718e120612ee1f904233f6a469a247b3d3a310f9d6`. Its final byte must be `0x00` so the harness evaluates the first 5275 bytes as QuickJS source with explicit length, which leaves internal zero bytes in-band. In the saved run this exact buffer parses to at least one `for..in` path that emits `OP_for_in_start`, reaches `build_for_in_iterator`, stays off the null/undefined return and `slow_path`, and then crashes on the `p->fast_array` read at `quickjs.c:15131`. The saved artifacts do not identify which of the witness's multiple `for`/`in` fragments produced that opcode or where the bogus pointer state feeding the cast at `quickjs.c:15129` was created.
